projects.title: Carryover: AI-Supported Daily Living App for Autistic Adults
bullets: Led user research with partner First Place AZ (a site visit and 2 staff meetings), and turned the findings into design changes, including always-visible safety cautions and adaptive help per step.
Wrote a literature review on prompt fading and executive function, and wrote the fading rules (when help fades or comes back, per step and per person) that the app follows.
Built a Python module that detects where users get stuck (4 patterns) from interaction logs, requiring patterns to repeat before acting, to avoid false alarms.
Wrote 4 task analyses and 10 skill cards grounded in research and USDA/FDA safety guidance, and built the Demo page's “Why this changed” explanations and “Help over time” grid.
Co-built a working prototype with simulated data (React, FastAPI, an LLM with code-based safety rules, and automated tests) on a 5-person team, and presented it at the Scottsdale Launchpad.

projects.title: Detecting and Correcting Social Bias in AI Question Answering (CSE 575, in progress)
bullets: Team project building a pipeline that detects biased answers from LLMs on the BBQ bias benchmark and rewrites them, while keeping accuracy on questions the context can answer.

Responsible for the data side: auditing and preprocessing BBQ, a loader that converts it into a general (text, label) format, and template-grouped train/validation/test splits so near-duplicate questions don't leak into the test set.

projects.title: Cyber Attack Detection in Water System Sensor Data (CSE 575, in progress)
bullets: Group project using the BATADAL water distribution system dataset to detect cyber attacks from sensor readings.
Did data cleaning and auditing, feature engineering, a Ridge regression baseline, and handling of partly labeled data.

projects.title: Trust in Advice: AI vs. Human Sources (Data Analysis & Written Report)
bullets: Analyzed 30,000+ human-AI interactions to study effects of advice source.
Modeled decision changes before and after advice exposure.
Found advice correctness as primary driver, with modest AI-related effects.

projects.title: Analyzing the Impact of AI on Stack Overflow Participation (NLP & Data Analysis)
stack: Python (pandas, NumPy, statsmodels, SciPy, Matplotlib, Seaborn)
bullets: Analyzed large-scale Stack Overflow data using Python to study changes in user behavior after AI tool releases.
Built time-series datasets and computed engagement metrics (answer rates, response time, retention) using Python.
Performed statistical comparisons and visualized platform-level trends.
Explored tag-based trends and basic NLP features to examine topic shifts.

projects.title: Predictive Analysis of Team Performance in Baseball using SAS
bullets: Developed a statistical model to predict team wins using historical baseball data.
Conducted EDA and correlation analysis on Minnesota Twins batting records (1998-2024, excluding 2020).
Built multiple regression models to identify key predictors of team wins, selecting runs and batting averages for a parsimonious model.
Addressed multicollinearity and validated model assumptions to improve predictive accuracy.
